newsitem.title: JAPAN: Newspaper says Japan plans change in stocks tax.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says Japan plans change in stocks tax.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry plans to overhaul the tax system for capital gains on stock trading, scrapping the option of taxation at source, a major financial newspaper reported on Sunday.

Under the present system a uniform 26 percent tax rate is applied to capital gains on stocks, but an investor can choose withholding tax, which is imposed at a fixed rate of 1.05 percent against revenues from stock sales, regardless of the actual amount of capital gains.
The system allows an investor to minimize tax payments by choosing the most advantageous system depending on investment results.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said the ministry has decided to end the option to ensure fairness in stock trading,
The newspaper said the ministry also plans to review the present 26 percent uniform rate, possibly introducing a progressive taxation rate system, to make taxation reflect investors' income.
Finance Ministry officials were not available for comment on the report and the newspaper did not say when the changes would come into effect.
